mainTopic: Why women are exempt from the prohibitions of rounding the head, destroying the beard, and (according to איסי) making a bald spot in mourning.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a צריכותא: the Torah needed separate verses to treat women like men in three areas, including כופר, because the reason behind one case does not carry over to the others. The גמרא then turns to the משנה, which exempts women from בל תקיף, בל תשחית and בל תטמא למתים. Impurity is easy: the פסוק says בני אהרן, sons and not daughters. For the hair laws, whoever is included in השחתה is included in הקפה. Women are outside השחתה, either by סברא (they have no beard) or because the פסוק says 'זקנך,' your beard and not your wife's. A ברייתא calling a woman's beard 'like a beard for all matters' leads אביי to bring the גזרה שוה of 'פאת פאת' from כהנים. After a back-and-forth, the גמרא concludes that the extra word 'פאת' teaches two things: women are exempt, and only a razor is forbidden. That ברייתא is then explained as being about the laws of נגעים. Finally, איסי teaches that women are also exempt from קרחה, since the פסוק says בנים. The גמרא explains why that limit applies to קרחה and not to גדידה, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Without the ransom verse, we would exclude women
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had only taught the other two cases, we might think כופר is paid only for a man, who is obligated in all מצוות, and not for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man, who is obligated in all מצוות: yes, the owner pays. A woman: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what mistake we would make if the Torah had not written the separate verse about כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man has more מצוות than a woman. So without a clear verse, we might have thought his life is valued in a way that requires כופר, while a woman's is not. The verse 'והמית איש או אשה' prevents that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: ransom payment owed when one's ox kills a person

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's conclusion. It is a 'we might have thought' (הוה אמינא) that the verse comes to reject.

phrases.english: A man, who is obligated in מצוות: yes,
phrases.notes: This is about כופר, the payment an ox's owner makes when his ox kills someone. He pays for a man.

phrases.english: a woman: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישׁ, דְּבַר מִצְוֹת – אִין, אִשָּׁה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא from the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows why each verse is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the כופר verse, we would say כופר is paid only for a man, since he has more מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כופר verse is needed to include women.

steps.title: The ransom verse alone would not be enough, so all are needed
steps.stepSummary: The reverse is also true. If the Torah had only taught כופר, we might say women are included there only out of pity because a life was lost. Then we would not extend it to the other two cases. So all three verses are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had taught only this one (כופר), we might say: since a life was lost, the רחמנא has pity on her. But in those other two cases I would say no. So all of them are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא by showing that the כופר verse could not teach the other two cases. It concludes that all three verses are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for including women in כופר (pity over a lost life) is special to that case. So it cannot be stretched to the other two areas. Each verse teaches something the others could not, which is why the Torah wrote all three.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One (the Torah) has pity
it is necessary (all the verses are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: Women are equal to men in the three areas covered by these verses. Each area needed its own verse, because the reason behind one does not carry over to the others.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this one:
because there is a loss of life
the Merciful One has pity on her,
but in those other two, I would say no,
phrases.notes: The other two cases from earlier where women are equal to men.

phrases.english: so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא begun in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three verses are needed, since each teaches something the others could not.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the exceptions for women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: women are obligated in all prohibitions except בל תקיף, בל תשחית, and (as the 'etc.' hints) בל תטמא למתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for 'do not round' and 'do not destroy,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's list of prohibitions that women are exempt from. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's general rule is that women are obligated in all לא תעשה prohibitions. These three are the exceptions, and the גמרא is about to look for a source for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: do not round (the corners of the head)
do not destroy (the corners of the beard)

phrases.english: Except for 'do not round'
and 'do not destroy,' etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: 'and do not become impure from the dead.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section, returning to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are exempt from בל תקיף, בל תשחית, and בל תטמא למתים.

steps.title: Impurity has a clear source; what about the hair prohibitions?
steps.stepSummary: The exemption from impurity is clear from 'בני אהרן': sons, not daughters. But where do we learn that women are exempt from בל תקיף and בל תשחית?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, 'do not become impure from the dead' is clear, as it is written: 'Say to the כהנים, the sons of אהרן.' Sons of אהרן, not daughters of אהרן. But 'do not round' and 'do not destroy': from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that one exemption has an easy source. It then asks for the source of the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בשלמא means 'this part is fine.' The verse about impurity speaks only to males. The hair verses don't mention men or women, so the גמרא needs a reason to exempt women.

keyTerms.meaning: do not become impure from the dead (a כהן's prohibition)

phrases.english: Granted, 'do not become impure from the dead,'
as it is written: 'Say to the kohanim, the sons of Aharon'
the sons of Aharon, and not the daughters of Aharon.
But 'do not round' and 'do not destroy': from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the sources of the exemptions just quoted from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for women's exemption from בל תקיף and בל תשחית.

steps.title: The two prohibitions are linked in one verse
steps.stepSummary: Because הקפה and השחתה appear together in one פסוק, whoever is included in השחתה is included in הקפה. Women are not included in השחתה, so they are not included in הקפה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Do not round the corner of your head, and do not destroy the corner of your beard.' Whoever is included in destroying is included in rounding. And these women, since they are not included in destroying, are not included in rounding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by linking the two prohibitions. The same people are bound by both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being written side by side ties the two laws together. Who is bound by הקפה depends on who is bound by השחתה. So once women are outside השחתה, they are automatically outside הקפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a woman may cut the corners of her own hair (פאות הראש) without violating בל תקיף.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Do not round the corner of your head
and do not destroy the corner of your beard'
whoever is included in destroying
is included in rounding.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי נְשֵׁי, הוֹאִיל וְלָא אִיתַנְהוּ בְּהַשְׁחָתָה,
phrases.english: And these women, since they are not included in destroying,
are not included in rounding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse links הקפה to השחתה, and women are outside השחתה.

steps.title: How do we know women are not included in destroying the beard?
steps.stepSummary: The answer in step 5 assumed that women are exempt from השחתה. The גמרא now asks for the source of that assumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that women are not included in destroying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the foundation of its own answer by asking where the exemption from השחתה comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole derivation depends on women being outside השחתה. So the גמרא has to prove that step before the argument is complete.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that they are not included in destroying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a premise used in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that women are exempt from בל תשחית.

steps.title: First answer: simple logic, since women have no beard
steps.stepSummary: One answer is a סברא: women don't have beards, so the prohibition of destroying a beard does not apply to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say a logical reason: they do not have a beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer, based on common sense and not on a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A prohibition about destroying the beard naturally applies only to those who normally have one. Women usually don't, so they fall outside השחתה.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)

phrases.english: If you want, say a logical reason:
for they do not have a beard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 with a סברא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women have no beard, so השחתה does not apply to them.

steps.title: Second answer begins: a proof from the verse's wording
steps.stepSummary: Another answer comes from the פסוק itself. The גמרא quotes the verse again, and the next step explains what it learns from the wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say a verse: as the verse says, 'Do not round the corner of your head and do not destroy the corner of your beard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second answer based on a verse. It quotes the פסוק and is setting up a point about its wording, which comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the same פסוק is quoted again, but for a new purpose: to read something from its exact words. In the verse, 'your head' (ראשכם) is plural and 'your beard' (זקנך) is singular. The explanation of that change continues past this point.

phrases.english: And if you want, say a verse:
as the verse says: 'Do not round the corner of your head
and do not destroy the corner of your beard'
phrases.notes: Notice that 'your head' is plural and 'your beard' is singular. The גמרא will use this right after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 6, alongside the סברא of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A proof from the wording of ויקרא 19:27, which step 9 completes.

steps.title: The verse switches to singular: 'your beard,' not your wife's
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'ראשכם' (plural) but then 'זקנך' (singular). This change teaches that the prohibition is about 'your beard,' not your wife's beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the verse changed its wording, we learn something. If the rule were meant for everyone, the Torah should have written 'the corner of your beards' in the plural. Why does it say 'your beard' in the singular? To teach: your beard, and not your wife's beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in step 8. It shows how the wording of the פסוק itself teaches that women are not included in השחתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק speaks to a group (ראשכם, plural), and the second half suddenly speaks to one person (זקנך, singular). The גמרא reads the singular as 'you, the man, with your beard,' which leaves out the wife. This gives a source from the פסוק, alongside the סברא of step 7.

phrases.english: From the fact that the verse changed its wording,
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 19:27, 'your head' is plural (ראשכם) but 'your beard' is singular (זקנך).

phrases.english: for if so (if it applied to everyone),
let the Merciful One write: 'the corner of your beards' (plural).
What is meant by 'your beard' (singular)?
Your beard, and not your wife's beard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the verse-based answer that step 8 began by quoting the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The change from plural to singular in the פסוק teaches 'your beard, not your wife's beard,' so women are exempt from השחתה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a woman's beard counts as a beard for everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a ברייתא says a woman's beard and a סריס's beard, if they grew hair, are like a beard 'for all matters.' Doesn't that include השחתה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And are women really not included? But a ברייתא teaches: a woman's beard and a סריס's beard, if they grew hair, are treated like a beard for all their laws. Doesn't that mean for the prohibition of destroying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that women are exempt from השחתה. It brings a ברייתא that seems to treat a woman's beard exactly like a man's beard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 and 9 said women are not included in השחתה. The ברייתא says a woman's beard is 'like a beard for all matters,' and the most obvious 'matter' seems to be the prohibition of destroying it. If so, women would be obligated, which contradicts what we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
A eunuch, a man who normally does not grow a beard
Is it not? (suggests the obvious reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא says women must grow beards. It only says that if hair actually grew, it is treated legally like a beard. The question is which laws that covers.

phrases.english: And are they not included?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A woman's beard, and a eunuch, who grew hair,
are like a beard for all their laws.
Isn't that referring to destroying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 7 and 9 that women are exempt from השחתה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that women are exempt from the prohibition of השחתת זקן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a woman's beard as a beard 'for all matters,' which seems to include השחתה, so women would be obligated.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא can't mean השחתה, because of 'פאת פאת' from בני אהרן
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא cannot be about השחתה. Women are exempt from השחתה through a גזרה שוה: the word 'פאת' appears both here and in the section about כהנים, and there women are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You cannot say the ברייתא is about destroying the beard, because we learn 'corner' and 'corner' from the sons of אהרן. Just as there women are exempt, so too here women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the exemption of women. He says the ברייתא must be talking about other laws, because a גזרה שוה shows that women are exempt from השחתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'פאת' appears in the general prohibition (ויקרא 19:27) and in the prohibition for כהנים (ויקרא 21:5). The כהנים section speaks to 'בני אהרן,' sons and not daughters, so women are exempt there. The shared word carries that exemption over to the general prohibition, so the ברייתא's 'all matters' must mean something other than השחתה.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there, so too here (the pattern of a גזרה שוה)

phrases.english: אביי said:
You cannot say it refers to destroying,
since it is derived from 'corner' and 'corner' from the sons of Aaron.
phrases.notes: The two verses are ויקרא 19:27 (for everyone) and ויקרא 21:5 (for כהנים). Both use the word 'פאת.'

phrases.english: Just as there, women are exempt,
so too here, women are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְהַשְׁחָתָה לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by limiting what the ברייתא can mean.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא's scope based on a גזרה שוה that exempts women from השחתה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'for all matters' includes השחתה, so women would be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא cannot include השחתה, since the 'פאת פאת' גזרה שוה from בני אהרן exempts women.

steps.title: If 'בני אהרן' covers the whole section, a קל וחומר would be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions אביי's approach. If 'בני אהרן' applies to the whole section, the Torah would not need a separate source. A קל וחומר would do: if כהנים, who have extra מצוות, exclude daughters, Israelites should exclude women all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we hold that when 'sons of אהרן' is written, it applies to the whole section, let the verse not bother with it, and we could learn it from a קל וחומר. I would say: if for כהנים, for whom the Torah added extra מצוות, only 'sons of אהרן' are included and not 'daughters of אהרן,' then for ישראל, isn't it all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the method behind אביי's answer. It argues that if his assumption is true, the law could already be known by simple logic, so the Torah's extra source seems unnecessary. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed that 'בני אהרן' at the start of the כהנים section covers every law in it, including the beard. The גמרא says that if so, a קל וחומר already gives the answer: כהנים have more מצוות than Israelites, yet even for them daughters are excluded, so surely Israelite women are exempt. The Torah does not normally teach something that a קל וחומר already gives, so the setup needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written about the whole section
Let the verse be silent about it
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (or the reverse)
Isn't it all the more so?

steps.whyThisMatters: This tests a basic rule of learning Torah: a separate source is not needed for something a קל וחומר already teaches. The סוגיא's answer in step 13 shows why the Torah's wording is still necessary.

phrases.english: And if we hold
that when 'the sons of Aaron' is written,
it is written about the whole section,
phrases.notes: 'Sons of Aaron' is in ויקרא 21:1, at the start of the section that includes the כהנים' beard prohibition.

phrases.english: let the verse be silent about it
and it would be learned through a קל וחומר,
since I would say:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כֹּהֲנִים שֶׁרִיבָּה בָּהֶם הַכָּתוּב מִצְוֹת יְתֵירוֹת –
phrases.english: If for כהנים, for whom the verse added extra מצוות,
it is 'sons of Aaron' and not daughters of Aaron,
for Israelites, isn't it all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סְבִירָא לַן דְּכִי כְּתִיב ״בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind אביי's גזרה שוה in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's assumption that 'בני אהרן' applies to the whole section, so a source is needed to carry the exemption to Israelites.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'בני אהרן' covers the whole section, a קל וחומר from כהנים (who have more מצוות) already exempts Israelite women, so the Torah's separate source would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Without the comparison, the exclusion of women would stop early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the גזירה שוה is still needed. Without it, we would say the topic was interrupted, so the exclusion of women in the כהנים section would not reach the beard prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the גזירה שוה, I would have said that the topic was interrupted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12, which asked why we need a גזירה שוה when a קל וחומר would be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בני אהרן' come right before the laws of טומאה. Without the גזירה שוה, we would say the exclusion of daughters covers only those טומאה laws, and the section 'breaks off' before the beard law. The גזירה שוה shows the exclusion of women reaches the beard prohibition too.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
The topic was interrupted; the earlier rule does not carry over to what comes after

steps.confusionAlert: 'הפסיק הענין' does not mean the Torah stopped talking about כהנים. It means the 'sons, not daughters' limit only applies to the first laws, the laws of טומאה, and not to the laws that come after.

phrases.english: If not for the verbal analogy,
I would have said: the topic was interrupted.
phrases.notes: He means the 'sons of אהרן' limit covers only the טומאה laws right after it, not the beard law later on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12 that a קל וחומר alone should be enough.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the source is needed: without it, the exclusion in the כהנים section would not reach the beard law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exclusion of daughters covers the whole כהנים section, so a קל וחומר is enough and the גזירה שוה is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the גזירה שוה we would limit the exclusion to טומאה, so the גזירה שוה is needed.

steps.title: Maybe the topic is interrupted anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even now, why not say the topic was interrupted, so daughters of כהנים would also be forbidden to destroy their beard?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, let us say the topic was interrupted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 13 and opens a new difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'interruption' idea is reasonable, it should still apply. Then the exclusion of daughters would stop at the טומאה laws, daughters of כהנים would be included in the beard law, and there would be no exemption to carry over to women in general.

keyTerms.meaning: Now too; even with what you said

phrases.english: Now too, let us say
the topic was interrupted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the 'הפסיק הענין' idea from step 13 into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the exclusion of women reaches the beard law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the topic is interrupted, daughters of כהנים are included in the beard law, so there is no exemption to learn from.

steps.title: The comparison is needed for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: If you say the גזירה שוה is what carries the exclusion to the beard law, that גזירה שוה is already used for another lesson. A ברייתא uses it to teach that cutting with scissors is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is because of the גזירה שוה, that is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'They shall not shave.' Might a כהן be liable even if he shaved with scissors? The פסוק says, 'You shall not destroy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible defense by showing that the גזירה שוה is busy teaching something else, and starts quoting the ברייתא that uses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might answer that the גזירה שוה of 'פאת' links the כהנים section to the beard law for everyone. The גמרא answers that this link is used to join 'לא יגלחו' (said to כהנים) with 'לא תשחית' (said to everyone). From 'לא תשחית' we learn that scissors, which do not destroy down to the root, are not included.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And if you say it is because of the verbal analogy,
it is needed for that which was taught in a ברייתא:
"They shall not shave";
one might think that if he shaved it with scissors he would be liable?
The verse teaches: "You shall not destroy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:27, said to all of ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge in step 14 by blocking the answer that the גזירה שוה carries the exclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the גזירה שוה of 'פאת' to exempt women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה already used to define which tool is forbidden is not free to teach who is exempt.

steps.title: Only a razor is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: tweezers and planes are not forbidden either, because the פסוק says 'shave.' The forbidden act must be both shaving and destroying, which is a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Might he be liable if he pulled out the hair with tweezers or a plane? The פסוק says, 'They shall not shave.' How does this work? It must be shaving that also destroys. That is a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which joins the two פסוקים to define the forbidden act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא תשחית' rules out scissors, which do not destroy. 'לא יגלחו' rules out tweezers and planes, which are not shaving. Only a razor both shaves and destroys, so this lesson depends on joining the two פסוקים through the גזירה שוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that the Torah prohibition on the beard applies to a razor, which both shaves and destroys.

phrases.english: One might think that if he pulled it out with tweezers or with a plane
he would be liable?
The verse teaches: "They shall not shave."
How is this?
Shaving that has destruction in it,
you must say this is a razor.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לִקְּטוֹ בְּמַלְקֵט וּבְרָהִיטְנֵי יְהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the גזירה שוה of 'פאת' is already used to define the forbidden act.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that joins 'לא יגלחו' and 'לא תשחית' to conclude that only a razor is forbidden.

steps.title: The extra word teaches two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the Torah only wanted the razor lesson, it could have written 'what is in your beard.' Writing 'פאת זקנך' adds the word 'פאת', so we learn both lessons from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק write 'what is in your beard.' Why does it say 'the corner of your beard'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the word 'פאת' is extra, so it can teach both the razor lesson and the exemption of women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A simpler wording, 'את שבזקנך', would have been enough to describe the beard. The Torah chose 'פאת', which creates the link to the כהנים section. Because of this extra wording, the גזירה שוה is used twice: to define the act (razor) and to exempt women.
steps.whatToRemember: Women are exempt from destroying the beard through the גזירה שוה of 'פאת'. The same גזירה שוה also teaches that only a razor, which shaves and destroys, is forbidden. Both lessons work because the Torah used the extra word 'פאת'.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
"That which is in your beard";
what is "the corner of your beard"?
Conclude two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 14 to 16 by showing the גזירה שוה teaches both lessons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows one source to teach two lessons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה שוה is used up by the razor lesson and cannot exempt women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because 'פאת' is extra, the גזירה שוה teaches both the razor rule and the exemption of women.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Women are exempt from the prohibition of destroying the beard, learned through the extra word 'פאת'.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא about a woman's beard teach?
steps.stepSummary: Since women are exempt from the beard prohibition, the גמרא asks what הלכה the ברייתא means when it calls a woman's or סריס's beard 'like a beard for all matters.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, a ברייתא teaches: the beard of a woman or a סריס that grew hair is like a beard for all matters. Which הלכה is that about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks what practical law it is talking about. This sets up מר זוטרא's answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that women are not included in the ban on destroying the beard. So 'like a beard for all matters' cannot mean the shaving ban. The גמרא needs to find some other law where a woman's beard counts.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman's beard (facial hair that grew on a woman)
a eunuch, a man who does not develop normally
for all their matters, in every way
for which halacha? What law does this matter for?

phrases.english: But then, that which is taught in a ברייתא:
The beard of a woman and of a eunuch
that grew hair
are like a beard for all their matters,
for which halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that women are exempt from the beard prohibition and asks what the ברייתא could then mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the ברייתא's 'like a beard for all matters' applies to.

steps.title: First answer: impurity of צרעת
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the ברייתא is about טומאת נגעים. A נגע in a woman's beard is judged by the rules for a beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: it is about the impurity of נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a first answer. The ברייתא is talking about the laws of צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נגע on the beard has its own rules, different from a נגע on regular skin. So a woman's beard would follow the beard rules, not the skin rules.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who answers the question
becoming impure from a צרעת sore

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
It is about impurity from leprous sores.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא teaches that a woman's beard counts as a beard for טומאת נגעים.

steps.title: The פסוק already says this openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a ברייתא would not need to teach טומאת נגעים for women, because the פסוק says 'a man or a woman... on the head or on the beard.'
steps.simpleTranslation: טומאת נגעים is written openly: 'A man or a woman who has a נגע on the head or on the beard'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר זוטרא's answer. It points out that the פסוק already includes women for a beard נגע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names a woman and a beard together. So the ברייתא would be repeating what the Torah already says plainly, and that is unlikely.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written openly in the פסוק

phrases.english: Impurity from leprous sores is written openly:
"And a man or a woman
who has a sore
on the head or on the beard"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר זוטרא's first answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that the ברייתא is about טומאת נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק already says this openly, so a ברייתא would not need to teach it.

steps.title: Second answer: purification of צרעת
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא changes his answer. The ברייתא is about טהרת נגעים: a woman's beard נגע can become pure by the beard rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר זוטרא said: it is about the purification of נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a new answer. The ברייתא is teaching about becoming pure from a beard נגע, not becoming impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק openly talks about impurity, but it does not openly say how a woman's beard becomes pure. So the ברייתא may be teaching that the beard purity rules also apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: becoming pure again from a צרעת sore

phrases.english: Rather, Mar Zutra said:
It is about purification from leprous sores.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: לְטׇהֳרַת נְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 19.

steps.title: Purification is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that טהרה is also obvious. If a woman's beard can become impure, it can surely become pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Purification of נגעים is also obvious! Since she can become impure, she can become pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer too. It says purity just follows from impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever can get a טומאה can also have the matching טהרה process. So the ברייתא would again be teaching something we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: something that can become impure can also become pure

phrases.english: Purification from leprous sores is also obvious:
since she is subject to impurity,
she is subject to purification!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר זוטרא's second answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא teaches טהרת נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Purity follows from impurity, and impurity is already written in the פסוק, so purity is obvious too.

steps.title: Needed: we might have split the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed. We might have read the פסוק in parts: 'man or woman' goes with 'head,' and 'or beard' goes back to the man alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought the פסוק is written in separate parts: 'a man or a woman who has a נגע on the head' is one part, and 'or on the beard' goes back to a man only. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא. It shows the פסוק is not as clear as it seemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 assumed the פסוק includes women for the beard. But we could have read the פסוק in separate parts, with 'or on the beard' going back to a man alone. The ברייתא tells us a woman's beard counts too, so the beard rules apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: split into separate parts, each going a different way
it teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא 'a woman's beard is like a beard for all matters' is about the laws of נגעים. Without it, we might have read 'or on the beard' as talking about men only.

phrases.english: It was needed,
because you might have thought
that it is written in separate parts:
"A man or a woman
who has a sore on the head" is one part,
and with "or on the beard"
we have come back to a man alone,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא לִצְדָדִים כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by showing the פסוק is not clear about women's beards.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a reading we might have used, which the ברייתא rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Or on the beard' refers only to a man.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman's beard also counts for the laws of נגעים, so the ברייתא is needed.

steps.title: Isi: women are also exempt from making baldness
steps.stepSummary: איסי teaches that women are also exempt from the prohibition of קרחה, tearing out hair in mourning for the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי taught: also for 'do not make yourselves bald,' women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. איסי adds another prohibition that women are exempt from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' adds קרחה to the beard prohibition, which we already saw women are exempt from. Now the גמרא will look for איסי's source.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who taught this ברייתא
the prohibition against making yourself bald in mourning

phrases.english: Isi taught:
Also for "they shall not make baldness,"
women are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי תָּנֵי: אַף בַּל יִקְרְחוּ נָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related exemption for women after the beard discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are exempt from the prohibition of קרחה.

steps.title: What is Isi's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason איסי has for reading the Torah this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of איסי, who expounds this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of איסי's teaching. This sets up the answer from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי gave a ruling but no source. The גמרא wants to know which words in the Torah leave out women.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Isi,
who expounds this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of איסי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that איסי uses to exempt women from קרחה.

steps.title: Sons and not daughters
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'You are sons (בנים) to ה׳... do not make baldness.' It says sons, not daughters, so the קרחה prohibition is only for men.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You are sons to ה׳ your God. Do not cut yourselves, and do not make baldness between your eyes for the dead. For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God.' Sons and not daughters, for קרחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives איסי's source. The word 'בנים' (sons) in the פסוק leaves out women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that forbids קרחה starts by calling us 'sons.' איסי reads this as limiting the ban to males. The words 'for קרחה' show that he applies this limit to baldness.

keyTerms.meaning: a bald spot made by tearing out hair in mourning

steps.whatToRemember: איסי: women are exempt from קרחה, because the פסוק says 'בנים' (sons) and not daughters.

phrases.english: "You are sons to the Lord your God;
you shall not cut yourselves,
and you shall not make baldness
between your eyes for the dead.
For you are a holy people
to the Lord your God";
sons and not daughters,
for baldness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by giving the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'בנים' (sons) in the פסוק that forbids קרחה leaves out daughters.

steps.title: Which prohibition does 'sons, not daughters' limit?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the limitation 'sons and not daughters' refers to קרחה or to גדידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it refers to making a bald spot. But maybe it refers only to cutting the flesh?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about its own claim. Maybe 'sons, not daughters' limits the cutting prohibition instead of the baldness prohibition. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two mourning prohibitions: 'לא תתגודדו' (do not cut yourselves) and 'לא תשימו קרחה' (do not make a bald spot). The word 'בנים' at the start of the פסוק could limit either one. Since גדידה is mentioned first, it seems at least as likely to be the one limited.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a bald spot by tearing out hair in mourning for the dead
Cutting the flesh in mourning for the dead
You say (introduces a claim that is about to be questioned)
Or perhaps it is only (offers another possible reading)

phrases.english: You say it refers to making a bald spot,
phrases.notes: He means the limitation 'sons, not daughters' from the end of the last step.

phrases.english: or perhaps it refers only to cutting the flesh?
phrases.notes: In the פסוק, 'do not cut yourselves' comes before 'do not make a bald spot.' (דברים 14:1)

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְקׇרְחָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִגְדִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the conclusion of step 26 that 'sons, not daughters' applies to קרחה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'sons' limitation goes on קרחה or on גדידה

steps.title: 'A holy people' covers cutting, so 'sons' must limit baldness
steps.stepSummary: Since 'כי עם קדוש אתה' already includes everyone in the cutting prohibition, the 'sons' limitation must apply to קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah says 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God,' that is said about cutting, and it applies to everyone. So how do I explain 'sons and not daughters'? It is about making a bald spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. A different phrase in the Torah already puts women under the cutting prohibition, so the 'sons only' rule must be about baldness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A holy people' describes all of כלל ישראל, men and women alike, and the ברייתא links it to גדידה. Once גדידה clearly includes women, the word 'בנים' cannot limit it. The only place left for 'sons, not daughters' to work is קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: For you are a holy people (דברים 14:2), which includes the whole nation
How do I fulfill or explain (a phrase that would otherwise seem to have no job)

phrases.english: When it says:
'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God' –
that is said about cutting,
phrases.notes: That is, this phrase puts the whole nation, women included, under the cutting prohibition.

phrases.english: so how do I explain
'sons and not daughters'?
It is about making a bald spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גדידה already includes women through 'עם קדוש', so 'בנים' must limit קרחה

steps.title: Why include cutting and leave out baldness?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own choice: why should women be included in גדידה and left out of קרחה, and not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what reason did you see to include cutting and leave out making a bald spot?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own answer. Why decide that 'a holy people' goes with cutting and 'sons' goes with baldness? Maybe it is the reverse. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both phrases are in the same passage, so the matching could seem random. The ברייתא now needs a reason to pair 'עם קדוש' with גדידה and 'בנים' with קרחה, and not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see, meaning what reason do you have (asks why one option was picked)

phrases.english: And what reason did you see to include cutting
phrases.notes: 'Include' here means applying the prohibition to women too.

phrases.english: and to leave out making a bald spot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 28 matched each phrase to a prohibition
steps.kashyaTarget: The pairing of 'עם קדוש' with גדידה and 'בנים' with קרחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the פסוק forces this pairing. The reverse pairing seems just as possible.

steps.title: Cutting is broader, so it is the one included
steps.stepSummary: גדידה applies whether or not there is hair, while קרחה applies only where there is hair. So the broader prohibition is the one that includes women.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include cutting, because it applies both where there is hair and where there is no hair. And I leave out making a bald spot, because it applies only where there is hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its reason. Cutting can happen anywhere on the body, so it is the wider prohibition. Making a bald spot can only happen where hair grows, so it is narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that the wider prohibition is the better candidate to include everyone, women too. The narrower prohibition is the better candidate to be limited to men only. That is why 'בנים' goes on קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: A place on the body where hair grows

phrases.english: I include cutting,
since it applies in a place of hair
and not in a place of hair,
and I leave out making a bald spot,
since it applies only in a place of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reason: the broader prohibition is the one that includes everyone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pairing seemed arbitrary and could be reversed
steps.terutzMaskana: גדידה is broader (any place on the body), so it includes women. קרחה is narrower (only where hair grows), so it is limited to men.
steps.whatToRemember: According to איסי's ברייתא, women are included in the prohibition of גדידה but exempt from קרחה, because גדידה is the broader prohibition.

steps.title: Maybe 'a holy people' is about scratching, not cutting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'sons, not daughters' could limit both קרחה and גדידה, because 'כי עם קדוש אתה' is really written about שריטה (scratching).
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that 'sons and not daughters' applies to both making a bald spot and cutting. And when the Torah writes 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God,' that is written about scratching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the whole approach of the ברייתא. Maybe 'a holy people' has nothing to do with cutting, so nothing puts women under the cutting prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 28 and 30 depended on 'עם קדוש' being the source that includes women in גדידה. If that phrase teaches about שריטה instead, then גדידה has no source including women. The word 'בנים' could then exempt women from both קרחה and גדידה.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (offers another way to read the source)
Scratching or scoring the skin in mourning

phrases.english: But say that 'sons and not daughters'
applies both to making a bald spot and to cutting,
and when it writes:
'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God,'
that is written about scratching!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 28 that includes women in גדידה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'כי עם קדוש אתה' teaches about גדידה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that phrase is really about שריטה, nothing includes women in גדידה, so 'בנים' could exempt women from both prohibitions.

steps.title: איסי holds scratching and cutting are the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: איסי holds that שריטה and גדידה are one and the same. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי holds that scratching and cutting...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge. איסי treats scratching and cutting as one thing, so a source about scratching is also a source about cutting. The rest of the sentence comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שריטה and גדידה are one prohibition, then even if 'עם קדוש' speaks about שריטה, it still includes women in גדידה. So the ברייתא's reading stands. 'בנים' limits only קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion
The תנא whose teaching about women and קרחה is being explained

phrases.english: איסי holds that scratching and cutting

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies two prohibitions as one, so a source for one serves as a source for the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עם קדוש' is only about שריטה, so women might be exempt from גדידה
steps.terutzMaskana: Since איסי treats שריטה and גדידה as the same, 'עם קדוש' includes women in גדידה too (answer continues)
